e-9816.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle Given Its Velocity
e-9816.problem: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $\mathbf{u}=(5\mathbf{i} +2\mathbf{j}) \,\textrm{km/h}.$ Find the speed of the particle.
e-9816.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =|5i+2j| \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+4} \\  & =\sqrt{29}\end{aligned}
$$

kilometers per hour.

e-9818.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
e-9818.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(\mathbf{i} -4\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\textrm{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{m/s}^2,$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$
e-9818.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
\mathbf u = \mathbf{i} -4\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = 2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} .
$$

Therefore, after $t = 5 \, \textrm{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(i-4j)+(2i+j)(5) \\  & =(i-4j)+(10i+5j) \\  & =(11i+j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9817.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle
e-9817.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0 \, \textrm{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $4\mathbf{i}  \, \textrm{km/h},$ and when $t=3\, \textrm{h},$ the velocity of the particle is $(7\mathbf{i}+15\mathbf{j})  \, \textrm{km/h}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
e-9817.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
\mathbf{u} = 4\mathbf{i}, \qquad
\mathbf{v} = 7\mathbf{i}+15\mathbf{j}, \qquad
t =3
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $\mathbf{a}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 7i+15j & =4i+a(3) \\ 3i+15j & =3a \\ a & =\frac{1}{3}(3i+15j) \\ a & =(i+5j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9819.knowledge_point: Finding the Time when a Particle Reaches a Particular Velocity
e-9819.problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{km/h}^2.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\textrm{h}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(3\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j})  \, \textrm{km/h}.$
e-9819.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}, \qquad
\mathbf{u} = -\mathbf{i} -\mathbf{j}, \qquad
\mathbf{v} = 3\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j}
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 3i+7j & =(-i-j)+(i+2j)t \\ 4i+8j & =(i+2j)t \\ 4i+8j & =ti+2tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $\mathbf i$ and $\mathbf j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}4=t \\ 8=2t\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $u=(i+4j)\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the speed of the particle, rounding your answer to two decimal places.
after.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =|i+4j| \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+16} \\  & =\sqrt{17} \\  & ≈4.12\,\text{km/h}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(5i+j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $3j\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=4\,\text{h}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=5i+j,\,a=3j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=4\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(5i+j)+(3j)(4) \\  & =(5i+j)+(12j) \\  & =(5i+13j)\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(-i+4j)\,\text{km/h}$ when $t=0\,\text{h}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i+j)\,{\text{km/h}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=6\,\text{h}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=-i+4j,\,a=2i+j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=6\,\text{h},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(-i+4j)+(2i+j)(6) \\  & =(-i+4j)+(12i+6j) \\  & =(11i+10j)\,\text{km/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-2i-8j,\,v=2i,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$

$$

Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=-i+7j,\,u=2i-5j,\,v=3i+2j
$$

into the equation above, we can attempt to solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 3i+2j & =(2i-5j)+(-i+7j)t \\ i+7j & =(-i+7j)t \\ i+7j & =-ti+7tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1=-t \\ 7=7t\end{aligned}
$$

which has no solution.

Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=i-2j,\,u=2i-5j,\,v=3i-j
$$

into the equation above, we can attempt to solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 3i-j & =(2i-5j)+(i-2j)t \\ i+4j & =(i-2j)t \\ i+4j & =ti-2tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1=t \\ 4=-2t\end{aligned}
$$

which has no solution.
